[LDET.2.2a] **Series backing state is part of "starting engine state."**
A series' running stats, deques, and signal backings are
engine state that lives outside working memory and is not serialised
across restarts ([LSER.9.2]). Byte-for-byte
replay of any rule that reads an aggregation therefore requires the
*same* series state at the start of replay — in practice either
(a) the recording began at engine-cold (empty backings), so every
sample re-absorbs from the stream in the same fact order and the
backings rebuild identically (the only v1-faithful path), or
(b) series state is captured into the starting snapshot. A recording
that starts against an already-warm engine cannot reproduce
series-derived facts, because the pre-recording history is absent
from the stream.
